recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-5847 in core unless Pharmacy later wants new general Dosage/MedicationAdministration guidance about duration semantics beyond this published DSTU1 clarification.
issue_request: FHIR-5847 was a Published/Persuasive Pharmacy change request asking to clarify MedicationAdministration.dosage.rate[x] because the old definition gave confusing infusion examples and did not clearly explain how Ratio or Quantity could represent rates such as 100 ml/hr.
initial_application: The issue was applied in the historical MedicationAdministration spreadsheet source. Commit 0c6541df609f5323c35e204e971168e5a89a4846 explicitly includes "#5847 change defn on MA.dose.rate" and replaced the old "200ml in 2 hours" / "100ml per hour" wording with the requested examples, including 100 ml per 1 hour, 100 ml/hr, 500 ml per 2 hours, 200 mcg/min, 200 mcg/1 minute, and 1 liter/8 hours.
additional_context: The active current build includes MedicationAdministration, and the migrated StructureDefinition source retains the substance of the FHIR-5847 definition. Related same-element decisions explain the current shape: FHIR-8238/FHIR-8502 supplied the rate-change comment, and FHIR-9603 later removed Range from MedicationAdministration.dosage.rate[x], leaving Ratio and SimpleQuantity as the current types. Searches found no current source copy of the obsolete confusing sentence and no relevant Zulip or Confluence record that changes the Jira/source conclusion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current MedicationAdministration.dosage.rate[x] definition already conveys the approved clarification, and adding the obsolete "default denominator" discussion from the 2015 resolution would be less clear than the current source.
